title: Seamless CSV snapshot partial recovery and tenant quarantine probes
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Problem: Large tenant usage exports occasionally fail mid-upload (OOM, transient network, webhook 5xx) leaving partial CSV blobs and inconsistent manifests. Current retry semantics either restart from scratch or rely on ad-hoc operator intervention which causes cost spikes and customer confusion. Goal: Implement a robust partial-recovery and quarantine workflow so exports can resume from the last validated chunk, quarantined tenants are isolated to avoid noisy neighbor effects, and operators have clear signals and remediation paths. Scope: - Streaming CSV generation with chunked, checksummed segments (S3 multipart compatible) - Durable per-tenant checkpoint manifests that record last successful chunk id, byte offsets, and schema version - Orchestration to resume failed exports from last checkpoint rather than restarting - Tenant quarantine mode: automatically lower concurrency and enable conservative retry/backoff for tenants with repeated failures; surface quarantine reason and duration in Console - Probes and health signals for export pipeline (snapshot TTL breaches, stuck checkpoints, export rate anomalies) - Backfill orchestration for missed exports that respects tenant priority and avoids overload. Out of scope: UI redesign of Console; changes to billing model for re-delivered exports.
acceptance_criteria: Export pipeline can resume a single tenant CSV export from the last validated chunk without duplicating rows
Failed export manifests are labeled and visible in the internal export inspector with quarantine state and reason
Quarantined tenants are automatically throttled and retried with exponential backoff; overall pipeline QPS remains within target SLO
Backfill job can process queued missed snapshots with priority-aware scheduling and produces idempotent outputs
End-to-end telemetry: per-tenant export duration, chunk success rate, checksum mismatch rate, and quarantine frequency are emitted to Datadog
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Drafted ticket and high-level design; flagged as P1 due to recurring customer incidents.
2025-02-21: Spike completed—validated multipart S3 approach using 5MB chunking; checksum model chosen (xxhash64) for speed.
2025-02-24: Prototyped checkpoint manifest schema (flat key-value manifest stored in S3 and mirrored in Postgres for quick queries). Open question: manifest write frequency vs. latency impact.
2025-02-27: Design review with infra and product; decided to implement conservative default checkpoint every 50MB or on explicit flush boundary. Marcus to own runtime integration.
2025-03-01: Implemented chunked writer and local resume in QA; observed a 2.3x memory reduction during large exports compared to naive in-memory CSV builders.

2025-03-03: Integration tests failing for webhook consumer idempotency—investigating race when webhook ack arrives during concurrent retry. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1447
notes: Trade-off: More frequent manifest writes reduce potential rework on resume but increase IOPS and cost; chosen default balances at 50MB with overrides per-customer SLA.
Edge case: Schema drift during backfill requires row-level schema tags in manifest; we will snapshot header checksum to detect incompatible backfill attempts.
Monitoring: added temporary alerts for 'export-checkpoint-staleness > 1h' and 'export-chunk-checksum-failures > 0.1%'
Operational runbook stub created in /runbooks/exports-partial-recovery.md for on-call remediation steps and manual resume commands.

Hook up quarantine state to Console API and expose reason + retry ETA

Run tenant-scale soak test with 200 concurrent exports (representative distribution of small, medium, large customers)
